summary: New geometry roadmap importing the existing symplectic, manifold and Lie foundations. This checkpoint source-decomposes a pointwise contact/Reeb prefix on the actual bilinear and symplectic carriers, with nonconstant rescaling and pointwise symplectization. The complete eight-stage design leads through contact and Lagrangian neighbourhoods and regular reduction to compact toric classification; its smooth and global proof dependencies remain explicit, not claimed supplied by the pointwise prefix.

nodes.title: Pointwise contact data
nodes.statement: For a real covector alpha and bilinear form beta on V, IsContactData(alpha,beta) means alpha is nonzero, beta is alternating, and beta restricted to ker(alpha) is nondegenerate. The zero-dimensional space has no such data; dimension one is allowed. This is a predicate on existing forms, not a contact manifold or an assumed Reeb vector.
hypotheses: V is a real vector space. Finite-dimensionality is not needed for the predicate.
proofSteps: Use the existing dual, kernel submodule, bilinear form and nondegeneracy predicates. Do not bundle a chosen solution to the Reeb equations.
In a smooth application the pair must be the actual values (alpha_x,(d alpha)_x). The predicate alone imposes no differential compatibility, smoothness or closedness.
acceptance: A nonzero covector with a degenerate horizontal two-form is rejected; nonzero alpha alone is not the contact condition.

sources.match: Pointwise refinement of the source definition; this does not supply a smooth one-form or its exterior derivative.

uses.how: Instantiated at the actual smooth one-form and its exterior derivative on each tangent space.
Supplies the horizontal perfect pairing and a normalized transverse vector.

The constructor and its evaluation retain precisely the original restricted form. Proof witnesses do not change the resulting data.

nodes.title: The transverse-line model
nodes.statement: For any existing real symplectic form omega on W, on V=R times W the pair alpha(t,v)=t and beta((t,v),(s,w))=omega(v,w) satisfies IsContactData. No finite-dimensional assumption is needed for this statement.
hypotheses: W is a real vector space with the given symplectic form.
proofSteps: The first projection is nonzero, as tested on (1,0). Its kernel consists exactly of pairs (0,v).
The given form pulls back along the second projection. Alternation and horizontal nondegeneracy follow from omega and the linear identification of W with that kernel.
acceptance: This is a pointwise model. It does not identify the derivative of the globally constant one-form dt with a nonzero omega.

sources.match: Explicit linear model of the source pointwise condition, not a false global derivative identity.

nodes.title: The Reeb equations have a unique solution
nodes.statement: For contact data on a finite-dimensional real vector space, there exists a unique r such that alpha(r)=1 and beta(r,v)=0 for every v in V.
hypotheses: V is finite-dimensional over R. The restricted space is therefore finite-dimensional as well.
No Reeb vector is part of the input data.
proofSteps: Choose u with alpha(u)=1 by rescaling a vector on which the nonzero covector is nonzero.

On H=ker(alpha), apply the EXISTING BilinForm.toDual of beta restricted to H. Let z be its inverse applied to the covector w mapped to beta(u,w). Its evaluation theorem gives beta(z,w)=beta(u,w). There is no new generic duality or covector-solver node.
Put r=u-z. It is normalized and annihilates H. Every v can be written alpha(v)r+h with h in H; alternation gives beta(r,r)=0, hence r annihilates all V.
For two solutions the difference belongs to H and annihilates H. Horizontal nondegeneracy forces the difference to be zero.
acceptance: In the transverse-line model the solution is (1,0); changing alpha to twice itself changes the normalization.

sources.locator: 11.1, Reeb equations and uniqueness, printed p.63
sources.match: The inverse-dual construction expands the pointwise source argument on the verified carriers. It is not a smooth-field theorem.

proofSteps: Use the existence theorem and its uniqueness to define r. All normalized-kernel properties follow from that theorem; any construction choices disappear by uniqueness.
acceptance: The value is nonzero because its alpha value is one.

nodes.statement: Construct the real-linear map P:V->ker(alpha), P(v)=v-alpha(v)r, where r is the proved normalized Reeb vector.

proofSteps: Normalization gives alpha(v-alpha(v)r)=0, so the value belongs to the actual kernel.
Linearity follows by expanding alpha on sums and scalar multiples. On the kernel P is identity; on r it is zero.
acceptance: P is a projection, not an arbitrary splitting chosen independently of beta.

nodes.title: The Reeb splitting
nodes.statement: Construct a linear equivalence V with R times ker(alpha) sending v to (alpha(v),P(v)); its inverse sends (t,h) to t r+h.

Normalization gives alpha(t r+h)=t, while the projection formula gives P(t r+h)=h. The other composite is alpha(v)r+(v-alpha(v)r)=v.
acceptance: The scalar factor is the normalized Reeb coordinate, not just an unspecified complementary line.

nodes.title: Recovering the form from horizontal projection
nodes.statement: For all v,w, beta(P(v),P(w))=beta(v,w). Thus the original two-form is recovered from its horizontal part under the constructed splitting.
hypotheses: V is finite-dimensional; the contact pair is fixed.
proofSteps: Expand both projected arguments. Terms with r in the first slot vanish by the Reeb equations; terms with r in the second vanish by the alternating skew identity.

nodes.title: First-order rescaling of exterior data
nodes.statement: For c in R and a real covector ell, define beta_prime=c beta+ell tensor alpha-alpha tensor ell using the existing linMulLin form. In a smooth application c=f(x) and ell=df_x, so this is the actual product rule for d(f alpha) at x, not merely c beta.
hypotheses: V is a real vector space with the given covector and bilinear form. The construction does not require c nonzero.
proofSteps: Use existing bilinear-form scalar multiplication, addition, subtraction and linMulLin. There is no new exterior-algebra carrier.
Evaluation is the displayed finite bilinear expression. Setting ell=0 gives c beta. Two successive first-order rescalings (c,ell),(d,m) give (dc,d ell+c m) by bilinear expansion.
acceptance: The construction is defined even at c=0, but the contact-preservation theorem must exclude that case.

sources.locator: 2.1, Definition 2.8 and the contact-form rescaling convention

nodes.statement: The rescaled form evaluates as c beta(v,w)+ell(v)alpha(w)-alpha(v)ell(w).

proofSteps: Apply linMulLin_apply to the two rank-one forms and expand their sum and scalar multiple.

sources.match: Explicit evaluation of the derivative-rescaling data.

nodes.title: Contact data under a nonzero rescaling
nodes.statement: If (alpha,beta) is contact data and c is nonzero, then (c alpha,rescaledForm(alpha,beta,c,ell)) is contact data for every covector ell.
hypotheses: V is a real vector space; c is nonzero. No finite-dimensional hypothesis is needed.
proofSteps: The kernels of alpha and c alpha are the same subspace; multiplication by c is invertible.

The rank-one correction vanishes on two horizontal arguments, so the restricted form is c times the original horizontal form. It remains nondegenerate. The whole new form is alternating by its evaluation formula.
acceptance: Negative c is permitted algebraically. Preserving an already chosen smooth coorientation requires a positive factor.
At c=0 the new covector is zero and the condition fails.

sources.match: The pointwise nondegeneracy proof retains the actual derivative correction.

nodes.title: Reeb vector under a nonconstant rescaling
nodes.statement: For finite-dimensional contact data and c nonzero, let Z in ker(alpha) be the inverse under the existing restricted BilinForm.toDual of ell restricted to that kernel. Thus beta(Z,w)=ell(w) for horizontal w. The Reeb vector for (c alpha,c beta+ell wedge alpha) is c^(-1)r+c^(-2)Z.
hypotheses: V is finite-dimensional; c is a nonzero real number; ell is any real covector.
proofSteps: The given inverse-dual evaluation proves the defining equation for Z; its value is uniquely specified.
The proposed vector r_prime has c alpha(r_prime)=1. For horizontal w, the rescaled-form expression is c^(-1)beta(Z,w)-c^(-1)ell(w)=0.
Every v is a multiple of r_prime plus a horizontal vector. The new form is alternating and hence also vanishes on (r_prime,r_prime). It follows that r_prime annihilates every vector.
Apply the proved uniqueness of the Reeb equations to the new contact data. No derivative of the factor is discarded.
acceptance: For alpha=dz-p dq and f=exp(q), at q=p=0 the new Reeb vector is partial_z-partial_p, not the old Reeb divided by f.
When ell has nonzero horizontal restriction the correction can be nonzero even at c=1.

sources.locator: 11.1, Reeb equations, p.63, with the contact rescaling convention of 10.1

sources.locator: 11.1, normalization of the Reeb field, p.63

nodes.title: Pointwise symplectization
nodes.statement: For contact data on V, construct an existing TauCeti.SymplecticForm on R times V with Omega((s,v),(t,w))=beta(v,w)+s alpha(w)-t alpha(v). This is the pointwise form beneath d(exp(t) alpha), without the harmless positive scalar exp(t). It does not claim a smooth or closed form has been constructed.
hypotheses: V is a real vector space with the given contact data. Finite-dimensionality is not needed for this construction.
proofSteps: Build the bilinear form with the existing pullback and linMulLin operations. Alternation follows by substitution.
If (s,v) annihilates all right arguments, test (1,0) to get alpha(v)=0. Testing (0,h) for horizontal h and using horizontal nondegeneracy gives v=0. Testing (0,w) with alpha(w)=1 then gives s=0.

The same separation on the other side follows from alternation. Package these proved properties in the existing symplectic-form carrier. The proof does not require finite-dimensionality or a Reeb vector.
acceptance: In dimension one this recovers the standard area pairing on a two-dimensional space.

sources.match: The source leaves the proposition proof as an exercise. The pointwise nondegeneracy proof above is supplied here; smoothness, exterior derivative and closedness remain SC.1 obligations.

uses.how: Supplies only the pointwise nondegeneracy of the actual form d(exp(t) alpha).
Provides the linear model for contact neighbourhood comparisons.

nodes.title: Evaluation of pointwise symplectization
nodes.statement: Omega((s,v),(t,w))=beta(v,w)+s alpha(w)-t alpha(v) for the constructed symplectization form.
hypotheses: V is a real vector space with the specified contact data.
proofSteps: Apply the existing bilinear pullback and product-of-covectors evaluation identities to the constructed form.
acceptance: The sign agrees with dt wedge alpha.

sources.match: Evaluation of the explicit pointwise form; no smoothness assertion is inferred.

nodes.title: Contact data under a linear equivalence
nodes.statement: For a real linear equivalence e:V->W, pullback of contact data (alpha,beta) on W gives contact data (alpha composed with e, beta(e(-),e(-))) on V.
hypotheses: V and W are real vector spaces; e is an actual linear equivalence.
proofSteps: Surjectivity of e preserves nonzeroness of alpha and alternation pulls back.

The restriction of e identifies the actual kernels. If a horizontal v annihilates all horizontal w in V, its image annihilates every horizontal vector in W by surjectivity of that restricted map. Nondegeneracy there gives e(v)=0, hence v=0. Alternation gives the right-sided condition.
acceptance: An arbitrary linear map is not enough: a noninjective map can produce a degenerate horizontal pairing.

sources.match: The pointwise coordinate-change argument preserves actual kernels and forms.

nodes.title: Naturality of the Reeb vector
nodes.statement: For contact data on finite-dimensional W and a linear equivalence e:V->W with finite-dimensional V, the Reeb vector of the pulled-back pair is e^(-1) of the original Reeb vector.
hypotheses: V and W are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
proofSteps: Evaluate the pulled-back covector and two-form on e^(-1)(r). They give normalization one and annihilation of all vectors by the original Reeb equations.
Apply reeb_unique to the pulled-back contact data. This is naturality for actual equivalent linear coordinates, not a claim about an unverified smooth pullback.
acceptance: The identity equivalence fixes the Reeb vector; compositions follow from the explicit inverse-map formula.

sources.match: Naturality is proved from the pointwise equations and their uniqueness, not imported as an unverified smooth theorem.
